text: I feel like this song especially, but this whole album is so much a reflection of their life and journey.  It brings to mind seeing an old musician, loved by all, but matured beyond the rave and craze that they loved and perfected.  You find them in an lounge, holding the instruments they have loved, caressing beauty from their battered forms.  They play one or two of the old favorites, showing that they still have that fire inside them, but this time they entice the room to join in the melody and bring them closer to the music.  Around these moments, they take that same skill and fervor and mold it into a groove that is still distinctly theirs, but less wildfire and more fireplace.  It is a warm feeling as they pour out the lessons they have learned and do that thing that they love one more time.

text: Great story behind this song. The Beatles were in India, and Paul met a Jamaican guy who became his friend. Paul said that he always used to say "Hey,  Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da, life goes on, man!" So he decided to write a song based on it. When they were recording the songs that they wrote in India, which turned out to be the "White Album," Paul, Ringo and George were in the studio trying to figure out a beginning to this particular song. They just couldn't find a way to start it, and didn't even have a tempo yet. Paul said they were waiting for John, who was late for the session to show up. Finally Lennon walked in and said..."Hey boys, what are we working on?" Paul and George told John about the dilemma they were dealing with about the track,  "Ob-La-Di, Ob-La-Da." They couldn't figure out a start to it, or a tempo to the song.  McCartney said John immediately went over to the piano, sat down, and ripped right into the piano intro you now hear at the beginning of the song...

Had cats and dogs there too

Oh those small rural towns and neighborhoods were the best!

I'd go back if I could, but due to medical (and honestly financial) reasons I rely heavily on public transportation, so small rural towns aren't an option for me anymore :/

I miss those days!

text:
Hi, stranger. I’m Potato.

I’m keeping my real name private. I don't know if it's safe to put it out there on YouTube.I’m writing this comment because I want to share a little bit about what I’ve been going through, and if possible, I’d really appreciate some advice or guidance. So, I guess I’ll start from the beginning.First, let me clear up my age so you can understand my situation a little better and maybe give me more relevant advice. I’m 19 right now.
Honestly, nothing in my life seems to be going right. Nothing. My studies aren’t going well, and I’ve been failing exams. It’s not that I don’t want to study or that I’m deliberately avoiding it. I actually want to study and do well. I just don’t know what’s wrong with me anymore. I can’t figure out where exactly my problem is or why I can’t seem to get myself together.Another thing is that I don’t have any friends.It’s not like I never tried. I did. I genuinely tried to make friends, but for some reason, I could never really fit in with people, or maybe they just never accepted me. Even when I was part of a group, I always felt like I was being ignored. I was always the person at the back of the line, behind everyone else. People would talk to me when they needed something, but otherwise, nobody really wanted to spend their time talking to me.
I always treated them well. I was good to them, and whenever I got the chance, I gave them my time and attention. But somehow, that still wasn’t enough for them to accept me.
And then there’s my family.Because of how badly I’ve been doing in school and my recent exam results, I feel like I’ve become the “loser” or the “failure” in my parents’ eyes. I know they probably don’t literally see me that way, but that’s how I feel. I’m grateful that they haven’t kicked me out or abandoned me. They still feed me three meals a day and take care of the basic things I need. But the things they say to me, the pressure, the criticism, and the stress that comes with it still hurt a lot.
I’m only 19, and honestly, I don’t even know what I’m supposed to do with my life anymore.
Lately, I’ve been feeling numb. It’s not exactly that I don’t feel anything. It’s more like there’s this heavy weight sitting inside my chest, and I can’t really explain it.
Sleeping has also become really difficult. I stay awake until 2, 3, sometimes even 4 in the morning because I just can’t fall asleep. Most nights, I end up listening to music and trying to distract myself.
Some people tell me, “You’re only 19. Your life has just begun. Everything will be okay.”
I know they mean well. I really do.
But honestly, sometimes I’m just tired of hearing that. Right now, I don’t feel like everything is going to be okay. I don’t know what I’m supposed to do, where I’m supposed to go, or how I’m supposed to get myself out of this situation.
So if anyone reading this has ever been in a similar place if you’ve ever felt completely lost, alone, behind everyone else, or like you were failing at life, but somehow managed to get through it and are doing better now please, if you can, share some advice with me.
Even a few words from someone who has actually been through something similar could mean a lot to me.

Thank you for taking the time to read all of this.

I really appreciate it.
author: @potato-w2j

text: you matter, and yes, you really do. You could live for 3 more days or 90 more years, so every day, be grateful and don’t take it for granted. I made that mistake countless times. Spend time with loved ones, hug, kiss, laugh, have fun, and don’t give a f*** about what others think. Ask your crush out, travel, live life to the fullest, and be yourself. It doesn’t matter if you’re gay, bi, straight, Black, White, Asian, old, young, rich, poor, female, or male—at the end of the day, we’re human. Your chance of being born is 1 in 420 trillion; that’s an unbelievably high number, which you can’t even begin to imagine how large it is. You are so lucky to be here. I spent the last 6 years worrying, stressing every day about the future, and unfortunately, I still do. I have suffered from horrible depression, and some days I feel like giving up, but I remember this: 2026 so far has been poor but better and there is hope, and, to be honest—relationships, friends, personal life have been mixed great things and issues —but I keep on fighting. I know it’s hard, but no one deserves to feel like I do, and that’s why I’m commenting. I try to remain hopeful. I wish anyone seeing this comment the best in life and strength to overcome any issues. Be kind to everyone, smile at that one person, ask how they are, spread kindness and not hate. I really hope this helps someone reading this, and thank you for taking your time to read ❤
